content:
maya: hey — prep question: customer call in 30m. where's the single pane to grab p95/p99 TTFT and tokens/sec sliced by model+route? want links + a short promql I can paste into the call notes

derek: Grafana overview: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/latency/latency-overview (panel: pxx by model/route). Jaeger search: https://jaeger.redwood.com/search?service=inference. Quick promqls you can paste into the call notes:
```
# p95 TTFT by model and route (5m window)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_inference_ttft_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, route))

# tokens/sec by model and route (1m window)
sum(rate(redwood_tokens_emitted_total[1m])) by (model, route)
```

joan: if the customer is on dedicated/different routing, add `customer_id` label to both queries. note: we also emit `redwood_first_byte_seconds` for pure first-byte checks (useful to separate network from decode).

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-142 created (priority: P2) — assigned to oncall.

derek: for tails use 0.99 with the same pattern: `histogram_quantile(0.99, ...)`. also useful to look at per-instance heatmap panel (hover to see sample traces).

maya: perfect — any dashboard that shows tokens/sec vs p95 correlation? would like to show correlation quickly on call

derek: yep: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/latency/correlation-tokens-latency . open the panel, set time range to 15m. if you want the raw panel metric: there is a correlation heatmap that uses `sum(rate(redwood_tokens_emitted_total[1m])) by (route)` vs the p95 promql above.

sahil: quick note on alerts — current p99 alert is pretty aggressive (fires at 1.2s p99 for all routes). for customer-facing routes we should use a rate-based suppression and a per-route threshold. suggestion: only alert when p99 > X AND sustained for 10m OR burn rate > Y. example rule snippet:
```yaml
- alert: InferenceP99High
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_inference_ttft_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, model)) > 1.0
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "p99 TTFT > 1.0s for {{ $labels.route }}"
```
Use `for: 10m` to avoid flapping; for canary routes set a higher threshold or tag with `tier=canary` and silence.

joan: also watch warmup/cold-start: `redwood_model_warmup_ratio` (if < 0.7 on a node, we see TTFT spikes). recommend adding that as a suppression rule in alertmanager for < 5m windows.

maya: great — can someone paste a curl to fetch a sample trace/log for that route? i may want to show one live

derek: quick curl to the trace logs (requires SSO token):
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $LOG_TOKEN" "https://logs.redwood.internal/api/v1/query?query=route=\"/v1/generate\"%20AND%20customer_id=\"acme\"&limit=5"
```
That returns the last 5 logs for that route; for traces use Jaeger link that pre-fills `service=inference` + `operation=generate`.

sahil: follow-up on tuning: if this customer is latency-sensitive, consider lowering batch_size for their route and enabling `kv_cache` pinning. batching config lives in service config -> routes -> overrides, and we can recommend `max_batch_tokens` down 20% for a trial.

maya: thanks all. @derek can you PR a small runbook snippet with the two grafana links + the two promqls and the alert example? i'll attach to the call notes and then ping the customer.

derek: on it, PR incoming in ~15m. :thumbsup:

joan: tagging the oncall FYI — if it pages during the call, mute non-customer routes and follow the runbook steps Derek will add.

maya: awesome — saved me a ton. will post call summary afterwards. :white_check_mark:
